title: Google Scholar e índice h en biomedicina: la popularización de la evaluación bibliométrica
extended_summary:
This paper is not the requested 2025 secondary-school writing study on AI-assisted writing feedback. Instead, it is a 2013 bibliometric review and comparative analysis focused on Google Scholar, Google Scholar Metrics, Google Scholar Citations, and the h-index in biomedicine. The authors aim to examine the characteristics, benefits, and limitations of these tools and to compare the h-index values they generate against more established bibliometric databases such as Web of Science and Scopus.

The paper’s approach is primarily a conceptual and methodological review, supplemented by an empirical comparison of journal and researcher h-index values in the field of Intensive Care Medicine. It does not study an educational intervention, writing instruction, or AI-generated feedback for students. Rather than testing a treatment, it analyzes bibliometric indicators derived from different databases and compares rankings across those sources using Spearman correlations.

The context is biomedical research evaluation, especially for journals and researchers in intensive care medicine. The authors compare 26 journals and 20 researchers using h-index values drawn from Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar Metrics, and Google Scholar. They report that Google Scholar tends to produce higher average h-index values than Web of Science and Scopus, but that the relative rankings of journals and researchers remain highly similar across data sources.

The main conclusion is that Google Scholar and its related services can serve as useful, accessible tools for information retrieval and bibliometric assessment in the health sciences, despite technical and methodological limitations such as lack of transparency, normalization issues, and vulnerability to manipulation. The paper argues that these tools have helped popularize bibliometric evaluation by making citation-based metrics more widely available beyond specialist audiences.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided paper is a bibliometric review about Google Scholar, h-index, and research evaluation in biomedicine, not an education intervention study. It contains no school-based treatment, learner sample, writing instruction experiment, or causal educational evaluation relevant to the requested secondary-school writing topic.
impact_tier_rationale: This paper does not report impacts on student writing, literacy, or any educational outcome. Therefore there is no extractable intervention impact for the target knowledge graph.
